findings.message: FLEET_HARD_DEADLINE now caps the delivery window (DELIVER_BY), but agent_budget is still `FLEET_AGENT_TIMEOUT - SECONDS`. The agent can therefore run past the point where delivery still fits before the Job's activeDeadlineSeconds. The fix covers the push loop, which is the case that was named, but not the agent run that comes before it. Fix: when FLEET_HARD_DEADLINE is valid, also cap agent_budget at `hard deadline - now - (delivery reserve)`, and compute it in the same place as DELIVER_BY so the two cannot drift. Add table rows for a pod that started late: delay 0, delay just above 120 s, and delay above 600 s.
findings.scenario: FLEET_AGENT_TIMEOUT=7200. The pod starts 500 s after dispatch (slow image pull or scheduling), and the agent uses its full budget. Then hard_left = 7200+600-500-180 = 7120, so DELIVER_BY=7120, which is before the agent finishes at SECONDS≈7200. No push is attempted, and the run records push-failed 'delivery budget spent' even though the remote is healthy. With a delay above 600 s, Kubernetes kills the pod during the agent run, so there is no record and no bundle. The README says the opposite: 'the pod still records the failure and saves the bundle before Kubernetes stops it'.

findings.message: The 600 s margin between the agent deadline and the Job deadline is now written twice. It appears once in activeDeadlineSeconds (manifest.sh around line 15, F_DEADLINE + 600) and again in the new FLEET_HARD_DEADLINE (`date +%s + F_DEADLINE + 600`). Compute the Job deadline once, for example `F_JOB_DEADLINE=$((F_DEADLINE + 600))`, and use that value for both activeDeadlineSeconds and FLEET_HARD_DEADLINE.
findings.scenario: Someone raises activeDeadlineSeconds to F_DEADLINE+900 and leaves the new line alone. The stamped FLEET_HARD_DEADLINE is then 300 s earlier than the real Job deadline, so the pod skips push retries it had time for and records push-failed. The opposite edit, lowering the margin, makes the pod plan retries past the point where Kubernetes kills it, so neither the record nor the bundle lands.

findings.message: FLEET_HARD_DEADLINE is a wall-clock time taken from the dispatcher's clock: a laptop in local mode, or the pipeline agent. The pod compares it with its own `date +%s`, so clock skew between the two machines shifts the delivery window by the size of the skew. Document this assumption, or make the pod treat a deadline that is implausibly far in the past or future at start-up as a flagged condition.

bundle_subpath keys the folder on the literal URL. The same Azure DevOps repo reached as https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_git/<repo> or as https://<org>.visualstudio.com/<project>/_git/<repo> gets two different folders, so a --retry dispatched with the other URL form does not find the saved bundle. The README says both forms are supported. Normalise the legacy host to dev.azure.com/<org>, or document that the URL form must stay the same between runs.
